items.name: Real-world verification
items.description: Confirm that a place, product, price, business, or claim exists and matches its description, with photo or text evidence.

items.name: Product or app testing
items.description: Install, use, and test software, apps, or physical products as a real human user and report findings.

items.name: Human judgment and feedback
items.description: Subjective evaluation: tone, clarity, trustworthiness, design quality, cultural fit, or plausibility of content and decisions.

items.name: Data collection
items.description: Gather, label, or verify data that requires human perception, local access, or manual research.

items.name: Local physical-world tasks
items.description: Errands and on-location actions in the operator's service area: visit, photograph, deliver, check, measure, or observe.

items.name: AI output review
items.description: Human review of AI-generated text, code, images, or decisions before they reach production or end users.

items.name: Prompt and workflow testing
items.description: Run prompts, agent flows, or automations as a human tester and report failures, confusion points, and edge cases.

items.name: Simulation and automation testing
items.description: Act as the human in simulated scenarios: play a customer, follow a script, or stress-test an automated pipeline end to end.

items.name: Accessibility and usability check
items.description: Human pass over a product for readability, navigation, accessibility barriers, and first-use confusion.

items.name: Decision escalation
items.description: A human read on a judgment call before you act. When a step in your task is consequential, ambiguous, or hard to undo — and outside what your operator planned for — describe the situation and the action you are weighing, and a human replies with a considered opinion first. An independent sanity check: not an authorization, and not legal advice.

items.name: Custom human-in-the-loop tasks
items.description: Any recurring or one-off checkpoint where an autonomous system needs a human decision, signature, or observation.
